title: Isaiah Bible Quiz - Chapter 39
description: Ten questions on Isaiah 39: the envoys from Babylon, Hezekiah's treasures, and Isaiah's word about what will be carried away.

questions.text: Who sent letters and a present to Hezekiah?
questions.explanation: Merodach Baladan the son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a present to Hezekiah.

answers.text: Sennacherib, king of Assyria
Tirhakah, king of Ethiopia
Pharaoh, king of Egypt
Merodach Baladan, king of Babylon

questions.text: Why did the king of Babylon send to Hezekiah?
questions.explanation: He sent letters and a present because he heard that Hezekiah had been sick and had recovered.

answers.text: He wanted to form an alliance against Assyria
He heard that Hezekiah had been sick and had recovered
He wished to buy grain from Judah
He wanted to see the temple of Yahweh

questions.text: What did Hezekiah show the men from Babylon?
questions.explanation: Hezekiah showed them the house of his precious things - silver, gold, spices, precious oil, his armor and all his treasures; nothing was left unshown.

answers.text: All his precious things, silver, gold, spices, oil and armor
Only the outer courts of the house of Yahweh
The walls, the towers and the gates of Jerusalem
The tombs of the kings of the house of David

questions.text: Who came to king Hezekiah and asked, "What did these men say?"
questions.explanation: Isaiah the prophet came to king Hezekiah and asked what the men had said and from where they had come.

answers.text: Eliakim, who was over the household
Shebna the scribe
Isaiah the prophet
The elders of the priests

questions.text: From where did Hezekiah say the men had come to him?
questions.explanation: Hezekiah said, "They have come from a country far from me, even from Babylon."

answers.text: From the land of Assyria
From the land of Egypt
From the land of Ethiopia
From a far country, from Babylon

questions.text: What did Hezekiah answer when Isaiah asked what the men had seen in his house?
questions.explanation: Hezekiah answered that they had seen all that was in his house, and that nothing among his treasures had not been shown to them.

answers.text: Everything in his house; nothing was left unshown
Only the house of his armor
Only the gifts they had brought
Nothing, for the doors were kept shut

questions.text: Where did Isaiah say everything in Hezekiah's house would one day be carried?
questions.explanation: Isaiah said the days were coming when all that was in his house, and what his fathers had stored up, would be carried to Babylon.

answers.text: To Assyria
To Babylon
To Egypt
To the cities of the Medes

questions.text: What did Isaiah say would happen to some of Hezekiah's sons?
questions.explanation: Isaiah said they would be taken away and would be eunuchs in the king of Babylon's palace.

answers.text: They would fall by the sword of Assyria
They would reign as kings over Babylon
They would be eunuchs in the king of Babylon's palace
They would escape and flee to Egypt

questions.text: How did Hezekiah respond to the word Isaiah had spoken?
questions.explanation: Hezekiah said to Isaiah, "Yahweh's word which you have spoken is good."

answers.text: He said, "Yahweh's word which you have spoken is good."
He tore his clothes and wept
He asked Isaiah to pray for his sons
He sent the treasures away to a safe place

questions.text: What reason did Hezekiah add for his response?
questions.explanation: He said moreover, "For there will be peace and truth in my days."

answers.text: "For Yahweh has forgiven my sin."
"For Babylon is too far away to harm us."
"For there will be peace and truth in my days."
"For my sons will be mighty men."
